docs.title: pystepdowner
docs.text:
A tool to enforce the Stepdown Rule (from Uncle Bob's Clean Code) in your Python files.

The Stepdown Rule states that code should be readable from top to bottom. Every function should be followed by those at the next level of abstraction so that we can read the program, descending one level of abstraction at a time as we read down the list of functions.

pystepdowner analyzes your Python files and rearranges functions and methods to adhere to this rule, prioritizing source-code call order and correctly handling complex dependency graphs.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
You can install pystepdowner as a global CLI tool using uv (recommended):

# Install from PyPI
uv tool install pystepdowner

# Or install from source locally
uv tool install .

Alternatively, you can install it into any Python environment using standard pip:

pip install pystepdowner

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: The CLI provides two main commands: fmt and rw.

docs.title: 1. fmt: Format and Print to Output
docs.text:
Use the fmt command to format a single file and output the result to your terminal. This is useful for previewing changes without modifying the actual file.

pystepdowner fmt -i my_script.py

docs.title: 2. rw: Rewrite Files
docs.text: Use the rw command to format and rewrite files. You can rewrite a single file or an entire directory recursively.

docs.title: Rewrite a Single File In-Place
docs.text: pystepdowner rw -i my_script.py

docs.title: Rewrite a Single File and Save to a New Location
docs.text: pystepdowner rw -i my_script.py -o formatted_script.py

docs.title: Rewrite an Entire Directory In-Place
docs.text:
This will recursively find and format all .py files inside the target directory.

pystepdowner rw -i src/

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
pystepdowner transforms bottom-up code into top-down code, putting high-level logic before the helpers it calls.

Before: 

def load_user(user_id: int) -> dict:
    return {"id": user_id, "name": "Alice"}


def format_user(user: dict) -> str:
    return f"{user['id']}: {user['name']}"


def user_controller(user_id: int) -> dict:
    user = load_user(user_id)
    return {"body": format_user(user)}

After running pystepdowner rw -i my_script.py: 

def user_controller(user_id: int) -> dict:
    user = load_user(user_id)
    return {"body": format_user(user)}


def load_user(user_id: int) -> dict:
    return {"id": user_id, "name": "Alice"}


def format_user(user: dict) -> str:
    return f"{user['id']}: {user['name']}"

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Topological Sorting: Correctly sequences nested function calls and handles mutual recursion.
  • Class Methods: Seamlessly reorders methods within a class definition.
  • Automatic Annotations: Automatically inserts from __future__ import annotations if an annotation dependency is moved below its definition to avoid NameError.
  • Comment Preservation: Retains module-level and function-level comments in their correct logical blocks.

docs.title: Cases
docs.text: Case names follow the pattern: {subject kind} subject -> {reference cardinality} {target kind} reference(s) via {reference form}.

docs.title: Functions
Function subject -> one or more function references
docs.text:
Subject: one module-level function. References: one or more module-level functions. Reference form: direct calls or lazy evaluation. Expected order: subject first, then referenced declarations in their first appearance order.

Before:

def d() -> str:
    return "d"


def c() -> str:
    return "c"


def b() -> str:
    return "b"


def a(key: str):
    # Direct call
    res = b()
    # Lazy evaluation
    mapping = {"c": c}
    # Lazy evaluation
    sequence = [d]
    return res, mapping[key](), sequence

After:

def a(key: str):
    # Direct call
    res = b()
    # Lazy evaluation
    mapping = {"c": c}
    # Lazy evaluation
    sequence = [d]
    return res, mapping[key](), sequence


def b() -> str:
    return "b"


def c() -> str:
    return "c"


def d() -> str:
    return "d"

docs.title: Function subject -> self reference and helper reference via direct calls
docs.text:
Subject: one recursive module-level function. References: itself and one module-level helper function. Reference form: direct calls. Expected order: subject first, then referenced helper declarations in reference order.

Before:

def leaf() -> str:
    return "leaf"


def helper() -> str:
    return leaf()


def recursive(items: list[str]) -> str:
    if items:
        return recursive(items[1:])
    return helper()

After:

def recursive(items: list[str]) -> str:
    if items:
        return recursive(items[1:])
    return helper()


def helper() -> str:
    return leaf()


def leaf() -> str:
    return "leaf"

docs.title: Function subject -> one class reference via annotation
docs.text:
Subject: one module-level function. References: one class. Reference form: parameter annotation. Expected order: subject first, then referenced class declaration.

Before:

class User:
    pass


def process(user: User) -> str:
    return user.__class__.__name__

After:

from __future__ import annotations


def process(user: User) -> str:
    return user.__class__.__name__


class User:
    pass

docs.title: Function subject -> nested function references via direct calls
docs.text:
Subject: one module-level function containing local functions. References: nested local functions at multiple nesting levels. Reference form: direct calls. Expected order: each local subject first, then its referenced local declarations.

Before:

def a() -> str:
    def b() -> str:
        def d() -> str:
            return "d"

        def e() -> str:
            return d()

        return e()

    def c() -> str:
        return b()

    return c()

After:

def a() -> str:
    def c() -> str:
        return b()

    def b() -> str:
        def e() -> str:
            return d()

        def d() -> str:
            return "d"

        return e()

    return c()

docs.title: Classes
Instance method subject -> one or more instance method references via direct calls
docs.text:
Subject: one instance method. References: one or more instance methods. Reference form: direct calls. Expected order: subject first, then referenced declarations in reference order.

Before:

class Greeting:
    def format_punctuation(self) -> str:
        return "!"

    def format_name(self) -> str:
        return "Ada"

    def greet(self) -> str:
        return f"Hello, {self.format_name()}{self.format_punctuation()}"

After:

class Greeting:
    def greet(self) -> str:
        return f"Hello, {self.format_name()}{self.format_punctuation()}"

    def format_name(self) -> str:
        return "Ada"

    def format_punctuation(self) -> str:
        return "!"

docs.title: Instance method subject -> one static method reference via direct call
docs.text:
Subject: one instance method. References: one static method. Reference form: direct call. Expected order: subject first, then referenced declaration.

Before:

class Greeting:
    @staticmethod
    def format_name() -> str:
        return "Ada"

    def greet(self) -> str:
        return f"Hello, {self.format_name()}!"

After:

class Greeting:
    def greet(self) -> str:
        return f"Hello, {self.format_name()}!"

    @staticmethod
    def format_name() -> str:
        return "Ada"

docs.title: Instance method subject -> instance method and static method references via direct calls
docs.text:
Subject: one instance method. References: one instance method and one static method. Reference form: direct calls. Expected order: subject first, then referenced declarations in reference order.

Before:

class Greeting:
    @staticmethod
    def format_punctuation() -> str:
        return "!"

    def format_name(self) -> str:
        return "Ada"

    def greet(self) -> str:
        return f"Hello, {self.format_name()}{Greeting.format_punctuation()}"

After:

class Greeting:
    def greet(self) -> str:
        return f"Hello, {self.format_name()}{Greeting.format_punctuation()}"

    def format_name(self) -> str:
        return "Ada"

    @staticmethod
    def format_punctuation() -> str:
        return "!"

docs.title: Class method subject -> one class method reference via direct call
docs.text:
Subject: one class method. References: one class method. Reference form: direct call through cls. Expected order: subject first, then referenced declaration.

Before:

class Greeting:
    @classmethod
    def format_name(cls) -> str:
        return "Ada"

    @classmethod
    def greet(cls) -> str:
        return f"Hello, {cls.format_name()}!"

After:

class Greeting:
    @classmethod
    def greet(cls) -> str:
        return f"Hello, {cls.format_name()}!"

    @classmethod
    def format_name(cls) -> str:
        return "Ada"

docs.title: Function contains nested function references
Function subject -> nested function references via direct calls
docs.text:
Subject: one module-level function containing local functions. References: nested local functions at multiple nesting levels. Reference form: direct calls. Expected order: each local subject first, then its referenced local declarations.

Before:

def a() -> str:
    def b() -> str:
        def d() -> str:
            return "d"

        def e() -> str:
            return d()

        return e()

    def c() -> str:
        return b()

    return c()

After:

def a() -> str:
    def c() -> str:
        return b()

    def b() -> str:
        def e() -> str:
            return d()

        def d() -> str:
            return "d"

        return e()

    return c()

docs.title: Function references
Function subject -> one or more function references
docs.text:
Subject: one module-level function. References: one or more module-level functions. Reference form: direct calls or lazy evaluation. Expected order: subject first, then referenced declarations in their first appearance order.

Before:

def d() -> str:
    return "d"


def c() -> str:
    return "c"


def b() -> str:
    return "b"


def a(key: str):
    # Direct call
    res = b()
    # Lazy evaluation
    mapping = {"c": c}
    # Lazy evaluation
    sequence = [d]
    return res, mapping[key](), sequence

After:

def a(key: str):
    # Direct call
    res = b()
    # Lazy evaluation
    mapping = {"c": c}
    # Lazy evaluation
    sequence = [d]
    return res, mapping[key](), sequence


def b() -> str:
    return "b"


def c() -> str:
    return "c"


def d() -> str:
    return "d"
